name: Ethiopia–Eritrea / northern Tigray
scenario: Cross-border escalation amid active internal fighting
confidence: Moderate for Tigray fighting; low for direct interstate clashes
summary: Continued fighting and Ethiopian force movements near the Eritrean border. Direct Ethiopia–Eritrea engagements remain disputed and unconfirmed in the reviewed reporting.
analysis: The best-documented change is the location and intensity of ongoing fighting and movement toward the border. An emerging interstate scenario must be kept separate from the already active Tigray fighting. Diplomatic mediation provides countervailing evidence.
next: Independent confirmation of an Eritrean military engagement; sustained cross-border formations; border closures or unusual evacuation/transport measures.
alternatives: Conflict among Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan forces can explain fighting and troop movements without a new Ethiopia–Eritrea war.

signals.title: Reported force movements toward Rama
signals.details: Critical Threats cites ACLED reports of Ethiopian troops moving from Adwa toward Rama on November 5–6.

signals.title: Direct border clashes alleged
signals.details: Accounts of clashes between federal and Eritrean forces were reported but could not be independently verified by Critical Threats.

signals.title: Chinese mediation contacts
signals.details: Separate diplomatic meetings with Ethiopian and Eritrean officials demonstrate continuing attempts to de-escalate.

signals.title: Mekele nighttime curfew
signals.details: Curfew reportedly imposed for city security after fighting; not proof of preparations for interstate hostilities.

name: Ethiopia–Sudan
confidence: High for diplomatic action; low for imminent attack
summary: Consular closures and reciprocal expulsions followed accusations concerning support for armed groups and drones launched across borders.
analysis: These are tangible, costly diplomatic actions. They are causally related reactions to the same bilateral dispute, not two independent war indicators. Direct interstate hostilities have not been established by this set of reports.
next: Verified cross-border state attacks or force concentration, travel/consular warnings, new reciprocal restrictions, independent border freight disruption.
alternatives: Diplomatic retaliation and information campaigns in the context of existing internal conflicts rather than a decision for interstate war.

signals.title: Reciprocal consular closures
signals.details: Ethiopia expelled Sudanese consular officials; Sudan closed the corresponding Ethiopian facility and expelled staff.

signals.title: Accusations about drone support
signals.details: Sudan alleged cross-border support for RSF operations; Ethiopia denied the allegation.

name: Afghanistan–Pakistan
scenario: New expansion of an existing cross-border war
summary: The two governments have engaged in cross-border attacks and fighting during 2026. The warning task is escalation beyond ongoing hostilities, not the onset of a new war.
analysis: Current attacks should be compared with the existing conflict baseline; an increase from zero is the wrong comparator. Need a measured weekly rate of strikes, casualties, and transport interruptions.
next: Multi-sector escalations, large-scale border closures and civilian evacuations, major diplomatic downgrade, independently corroborated unusual deployments.
alternatives: Counterinsurgency-driven cross-border actions that do not develop into sustained conventional interstate war.

signals.title: Border mortar and drone strike accusations
signals.details: CFR chronology cites Pakistani allegations of mortar fire and Taliban allegations of Pakistani drone strikes.

signals.title: Emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
signals.details: Pakistan imposed emergency rule amid an internal political-security dispute; not an independent indicator of a new interstate offensive.

name: DR Congo–Rwanda / Kivu
confidence: High for fighting; lower for new direct interstate attack
summary: Continued fighting and additional sanctions against Rwandan defense-linked entities coexist with security-coordination diplomacy.
analysis: Armed violence is persistent, while the October review reported no operationally significant movement in key sectors. Sanctions and diplomatic meetings may reflect conflict management rather than a new imminent escalation.
next: Independently verified new direct Rwandan intervention, extraordinary cross-border deployments, major ceasefire collapse or unexpected evacuation orders.
alternatives: Continuing proxy conflict and enforcement measures without transition to overt conventional interstate war.

signals.title: U.S. sanctions against Rwandan Ministry of Defense
signals.details: Critical Threats reports U.S. sanctions alleging support for M23-linked forces.

signals.title: Joint security coordination meeting
signals.details: DRC, Rwanda and other participants continued formal military-security discussions.

signals.title: Continued fighting in South Kivu
signals.details: Review documented combat but no operationally significant changes in its principal fronts.

name: Thailand–Cambodia
scenario: Ceasefire failure and renewed border combat
confidence: High for continuing dispute; low for imminent resumed combat
summary: Ceasefire is in effect but strained. Border issues persist, and officials continue military-level coordination.
analysis: A cessation of major fighting is a meaningful counter-signal. Political disputes and defensive measures need to be distinguished from concrete preparations to breach the ceasefire.
next: New corroborated border firing, collapse of military talks, emergency protective measures, atypical border crossing restrictions.
alternatives: Domestic political posturing and difficult negotiations inside a still-functioning ceasefire.

signals.title: Bilateral military implementation talks
signals.details: Military representatives discussed implementation of the December 2025 ceasefire.

signals.title: Continuing disputes over temple and maritime claims
signals.details: The parties disagree over border sites and overlapping Gulf of Thailand maritime claims.

name: Russia–NATO
scenario: Major conventional or limited hybrid escalation
summary: Poland's localized near-term security warning raises hybrid concern; NATO's public conventional-war assessment remains distinct.
analysis: One theater contains separate scenarios with different lead times. A specific sabotage warning should not spill over into an unsupported conventional-invasion warning.
next: New independent evidence of coordinated sabotage; major combined-arms concentration for conventional scenario.
alternatives: Defensive precautions may deter or prevent incidents; suspicious observations can be innocuous.

signals.title: Polish sabotage/provocation warning
signals.details: Poland issued localized protective measures concerning potential early-November sabotage or provocations.

signals.title: NATO finds no imminent conventional threat
signals.details: NATO secretary general said no imminent major attack buildup was observed.

name: U.S.–Iran / Hormuz
scenario: Wider escalation in ongoing armed conflict
confidence: High for ongoing conflict; uncertain for new major escalation
summary: Shipping disruption and military confrontation are already established; the relevant change is any new expansion of scope, intensity, or geography.
analysis: Historic maritime disruption is severe but persistent. AIBA must detect changes relative to the current wartime regime rather than repeatedly score the prewar-to-war transition.
next: New independent commercial transit acceleration/deceleration, broader protective evacuations, verified expansion of hostilities.
alternatives: Deterrent reinforcement or localized strikes may occur without a new theater-wide campaign.

signals.title: Iranian proposal via Qatar
signals.details: A new diplomatic proposal was delivered; central disagreements remained unresolved.

signals.title: Warnings to partners and force reinforcement
signals.details: AP reported U.S. regional reinforcement and partner alerts about possible renewed attacks.

name: Taiwan Strait
scenario: Blockade, quarantine or major armed attack
confidence: High for measured activity; low for timing
summary: October saw increases in coast guard and coordinated readiness patrols but a decrease in aggregate PLA aircraft sorties.
analysis: Force mix has shifted, yet broad maritime commerce has not demonstrated collapse. Distinguish gray-zone coercion from blockade preparations.
next: Sustained multi-day vessel concentration plus unprecedented commercial departures, extraordinary maritime restrictions and concrete logistical signatures.
alternatives: Persistent coercive activity without a decision to initiate a blockade.

signals.title: PLA aircraft sorties decrease
signals.details: October monthly PLA sorties declined from 255 in September to 232.

signals.title: Coast guard incursions increase
signals.details: Coast guard incursions rose from seven in September to twelve in October.

name: Korean Peninsula
scenario: Border clash or major inter-Korean escalation
confidence: Moderate for activity; low for timing
summary: North Korea's testing and hostile public statements have increased without a verified major offensive readiness sequence.
analysis: Weapons testing is often a recurring regime, not a countdown. Require extraordinary readiness or protective changes to elevate beyond an activity watch.
next: Unexpected large-scale offensive deployments, emergency civilian protective measures, or major airspace restrictions.
alternatives: Testing and political coercion rather than attack execution.

signals.title: Multiple weapons launches in one month
signals.details: Reuters reported North Korea's fourth recent weapons launch.

name: Ethiopia–Kenya / Moyale spillover
scenario: Civil conflict spillover and refugee movement across Ethiopia–Kenya border
trajectory: Persisting humanitarian pressure; no interstate attack indication
confidence: High on displacement; limited on armed escalation
summary: Fighting in Ethiopian Moyale since about October 22 caused significant cross-border displacement. UNHCR reported local estimates up to 50,000 people crossing by October 28; Kenyan security officials described additional measures November 6. Numbers remain preliminary.
analysis: Independent humanitarian and Kenyan government statements confirm consequential spillover. The later protective measures are an institutional response to known fighting, NOT independent proof of planned military action against Kenya. Critical AIBA warning: count actual displacement and protection costs; do not confuse response with pre-war leading behavior.
next: Monitor UNHCR registration updates against estimates, verification of new cross-border armed incursions, Kenyan changes to civilian protection, and independent commercial-transport disruptions. Promote an interstate scenario only with evidence about state-directed attacks.
alternatives: Population flight may reflect localized intra-Ethiopian fighting and civilian risk avoidance without expansion into an interstate confrontation. Reporting and registrations lag actual movements.

signals.title: Fighting reported around Ethiopian Moyale
signals.details: October 22 is an approximate onset reported later by Kenyan authorities and UNHCR; do not equate observation date with contemporary discovery on Oct 22.

signals.title: UNHCR reports substantial cross-border movement
signals.details: UNHCR says local authorities estimate up to 50,000 crossed since October 22; registration incomplete. Agency announces relief response and appeal of $8.9m for support up to 50,000. This is lagging/confirmatory behavior, not a leading forecast.

signals.title: Kenyan police announce border security measures
signals.details: Kenya police inspector general described security deployment and protection for Moyale/Marsabit after displacement; response to existing crisis rather than prediction of a new interstate offensive.
